examples.en: My nose tip turned red like a strawberry because of the cold.
My glasses keep sliding down to the tip of my nose.
The smell of tasty bread tickles my nose.
The cat lightly licked the tip of my nose.

examples.ko: 너무 추워서 이불을 코끝까지 덮고 잤어요.
examples.en: It was so cold that I slept with the blanket pulled up to my nose.

examples.ko: 코끝에 땀이 맺힐 만큼 열심히 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I ran so hard that sweat beaded on the tip of my nose.

explain: '코'가 얼굴의 코 전체라면 '코끝'은 맨 끝부분만 콕 집어 말해요. 추워서 빨개지거나 시릴 때, 냄새가 스칠 때처럼 코끝에서 느끼는 감각을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I got choked up while reading the letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬프거나 감동해서 눈물이 날 것 같을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so sad or moved that you feel close to tears.

explain_en: While '코' is the whole nose, '코끝' points to just the very tip. It fits sensations felt at the tip, such as the nose turning red or stinging from the cold, or a smell brushing past.

examples.en: My eyesight is bad, so I wear contact lenses.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 콘택트렌즈를 꼭 빼야 해요.
examples.en: You must take out your contact lenses before going to sleep.
My contact lens fell out of my eye while I was exercising.
Contact lenses are more comfortable than glasses, so I use them often.
My eyes keep getting dry because of my contact lenses.

examples.ko: 새 콘택트렌즈를 사러 안경원에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I am going to the optical shop to buy new contact lenses.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 줄여서 그냥 '렌즈'라고 많이 말해요. 안경은 '쓰다'지만 렌즈는 '끼다', 뺄 때는 '빼다'를 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people often shorten it to just '렌즈'. Glasses go with '쓰다', but lenses go with '끼다' (put in), and '빼다' for taking them out.

examples.en: It was raining a lot, so I called a taxi.
They say the taxi will arrive within five minutes.
Late at night, it is easier to book a call taxi.
How much would it cost to go to the airport by call taxi?

examples.ko: 할머니께서 병원에 가실 때 콜택시를 이용해요.
examples.en: My grandmother uses a call taxi when she goes to the hospital.
I sent the address to the call taxi driver by text message.

explain: 길에서 손을 들어 잡는 택시와 달리, 전화나 앱으로 '부르는' 택시예요. 그래서 '콜택시를 부르다/예약하다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: Unlike a taxi you flag down on the street, this is a taxi you summon by phone or app. That is why it pairs with verbs like '부르다' (call) and '예약하다' (book).

examples.en: Dust got in and the inside of my nose itches.
I caught a cold and my nose is completely blocked.
I feel like something got inside my nose.
In dry winter, the inside of your nose easily dries out.
The doctor examined the inside of my nose.
The spicy smell rushes all the way up into my nose.

explain: '코'와 '속'이 합쳐진 말이라 소리 낼 때 [콛쏙]처럼 '쏙'으로 세게 나요. 감기, 먼지, 건조함처럼 코 안쪽이 불편할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is '코' plus '속', and it is pronounced [콛쏙] with a tense 'ssok' sound. It is used when something feels uncomfortable inside the nose, such as with a cold, dust or dryness.

examples.en: The child drew a picture on the wallpaper with crayons.

examples.ko: 동생이 벽에 선을 그어서 크레파스를 뺏겼어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling drew lines on the wall and had the crayons taken away.
The crayon broke, so I bought a new one.
I put a twelve-color crayon set in my bag.
When I was little, I liked the smell of crayons.
Could you lend me your crayons?

explain: 연필처럼 깎아서 쓰는 '색연필'과 달리, 크레파스는 문질러서 넓게 칠하는 그림 도구예요. 주로 어린이 미술 시간에 쓰는 물건이라 '크레파스로 칠하다/그리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike colored pencils that you sharpen, a cray-pas is rubbed on to color wide areas. It is mostly an item for children's art class, so you say '크레파스로 칠하다/그리다'.

examples.en: On Christmas Eve, I eat cake with my family.
I hope it snows on Christmas Eve.
I decided to meet my friends on the evening of Christmas Eve.
We first met on Christmas Eve.
It is Christmas Eve, so there are many people on the street.
Reservations for Christmas Eve are already full.

explain: 12월 24일을 말하고, 줄여서 그냥 '이브'라고도 해요. 한국에서는 크리스마스 당일만큼 이브에도 약속을 잡거나 모임을 하는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: It means December 24th and is often shortened to just '이브'. In Korea many people make plans or hold gatherings on the eve as much as on Christmas Day itself.

examples.en: I hung a star on top of the Christmas tree.
The child is busy decorating the Christmas tree.
A huge Christmas tree was set up in front of the church.
I placed a small Christmas tree in the living room.
Little lights twinkled on the Christmas tree.

examples.ko: 백화점 앞 크리스마스트리 옆에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo next to the Christmas tree in front of the department store.

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 '트리'라고도 해요. '꾸미다, 세우다, 달다'처럼 장식하고 세우는 동사와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: In speech it is often shortened to just '트리'. It pairs well with verbs for decorating and setting up, such as '꾸미다', '세우다' and '달다'.

examples.en: I squirt tomato ketchup on my fries and eat them.
We are almost out of tomato ketchup.
I drew a heart on the omelet rice with tomato ketchup.
Sorry, could you give me a little more tomato ketchup?

examples.ko: 아이들은 소시지를 토마토케첩에 듬뿍 찍어 먹어요.
examples.en: The kids dip their sausages generously in tomato ketchup.
I got tomato ketchup on my clothes, so I have to wash them.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 그냥 '케첩'이라고 해요. 찍어 먹을 때는 '찍다', 짜서 뿌릴 때는 '뿌리다'나 '짜다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk it is usually shortened to just '케첩'. Use '찍다' for dipping and '뿌리다' or '짜다' for squirting it on.

examples.en: In the morning I toast bread in the toaster.
The finished bread popped out of the toaster.

examples.ko: 저는 매일 토스터로 빵을 구워 먹어요.
examples.en: I toast bread with a toaster every day.

examples.ko: 토스터가 고장 나서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The toaster broke, so I need to buy a new one.

examples.ko: 작은 토스터라서 한 번에 두 장만 구울 수 있어요.
examples.en: It is a small toaster, so it can only toast two slices at a time.

examples.ko: 이 토스터는 빵이 잘 타지 않아요.
examples.en: Bread doesn't burn easily in this toaster.

explain: 기계는 '토스터', 구운 빵으로 만든 음식은 '토스트'로 달라요. 빵은 '토스터에 굽다'처럼 '굽다'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: The machine is a '토스터', while the food made from toasted bread is '토스트'. Bread goes with '굽다', as in '토스터에 굽다'.

examples.en: When the green light comes on, we cross the street.
The crosswalk signal changed to green.
The green light is blinking, so don't run.
I am waiting for the green light at the crosswalk.
You stop at the red light and go at the green light.
The light was green but a car didn't stop, so I was startled.

explain: 신호등의 초록색도 한국어에서는 보통 '파란불'이라고 말해요. 반대는 '빨간불'이고, 신호는 '켜지다/바뀌다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: The new business finally got the go-ahead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 잘 풀릴 조짐이 보인다는 비유예요. 반대로 '빨간불이 켜지다'는 문제가 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech meaning things are starting to look promising. The opposite, '빨간불이 켜지다', means trouble has appeared.

explain_en: Even though the traffic signal is green, Korean speakers usually call it '파란불'. The opposite is '빨간불', and it goes with verbs like '켜지다' and '바뀌다'.

en: part-time job; side job; student job; moonlighting

examples.en: During vacation I work part-time at a cafe.

examples.ko: 방학 때 할 파트타임 일을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a part-time job to do during vacation.
I only work part-time on weekends.
Since it is part-time, my schedule is fairly flexible.
This shop is hiring part-time staff.
I earn my pocket money from my part-time pay.

explain: 학생이나 젊은 사람이 일할 때는 '알바(아르바이트)'라는 말을 더 많이 해요. '파트타임'은 시간제로 일한다는 근무 방식을 말할 때 잘 쓰고, 반대는 '풀타임'이에요.
explain_en: When students or young people talk about such work, they more often say '알바' (아르바이트). '파트타임' fits when you mean the working style of limited hours, and its opposite is '풀타임'.

examples.ko: 생일 선물로 받은 시계를 팔목에 찼어요.
examples.en: I put on the watch I got as a birthday present on my wrist.
I hurt my wrist when I fell on the stairs.
My wrist hurts, so it is hard to use a mouse.
My friend grabbed my wrist tightly.
The sleeves are short, so my whole wrist shows.
I rolled my sleeves up to the wrist.

explain: '손목'도 같은 부분을 가리켜서 시계나 팔찌 이야기에서 둘 다 들을 수 있어요. 시계는 '차다'를 써서 '팔목에 차다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '손목' points to the same part, so you may hear both when people talk about watches or bracelets. A watch goes with '차다', as in '팔목에 차다'.

examples.en: In the hot summer, I think of patbingsu.

examples.ko: 우리 팥빙수 하나 시켜서 나눠 먹어요.
examples.en: Let's order one patbingsu and share it.
This cafe is famous for its strawberry patbingsu.

examples.ko: 팥빙수를 너무 빨리 먹으면 머리가 아파요.
examples.en: If you eat patbingsu too fast, you get a headache.
They put rice cake and fruit on top of the patbingsu.

examples.ko: 할머니가 만들어 주신 팥빙수가 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The patbingsu my grandmother made for me is the tastiest.

explain: [팓삥수]처럼 소리 나요. 얼음 위에 단팥을 올린 여름 디저트라서 '먹기 전에 잘 비벼요'라고 말하는 일이 많고, 과일을 올리면 '과일빙수'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is pronounced [팓삥수]. It is a summer dessert with sweet red beans on shaved ice, and people often say to mix it well before eating. With fruit on top it can be called '과일빙수'.

examples.ko: 우산이 잘 펴지지 않아서 비를 맞았어요.
examples.en: The umbrella wouldn't open properly, so I got wet.

examples.ko: 다리미로 누르면 주름이 쫙 펴지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the wrinkles smooth out when you press them with an iron.

examples.ko: 구겨진 종이가 물에 닿으면 저절로 펴지기도 해요.
examples.en: Crumpled paper sometimes flattens out by itself when it touches water.

examples.ko: 마음이 놓이니까 찡그린 얼굴이 펴지고 웃음이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Once I felt relieved, my frowning face relaxed and I smiled.

examples.ko: 이 소파는 버튼을 누르면 침대처럼 펴지는 거예요.
examples.en: This sofa unfolds like a bed when you press the button.
I couldn't straighten my back, so I went to the hospital.

explain: '펴다'는 내가 펴는 것이고, '펴지다'는 접히거나 구겨진 것이 저절로 또는 어떤 힘으로 펴진다는 느낌이에요. 주름, 우산, 허리, 얼굴처럼 접히거나 굽은 것에 잘 써요.

phrases.example: 취직한 뒤로 우리 집 형편이 많이 펴졌어요.
phrases.en: Since I got a job, our family's circumstances have improved a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렵던 살림이 나아져서 여유가 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that a tight financial situation has improved and there is some breathing room.

explain_en: '펴다' is you opening something, while '펴지다' is the folded or crumpled thing becoming open or flat on its own or by some force. It suits wrinkles, umbrellas, backs and faces, things that are folded or bent.

examples.en: I wrote a handwritten letter on pretty letter paper.
I ran out of letter paper, so I went to the stationery store.
I bought a pack of flower-patterned letter paper.

examples.ko: 편지지 두 장에 하고 싶은 말을 가득 적었어요.
examples.en: I filled two sheets of letter paper with what I wanted to say.

examples.ko: 이 편지지는 종이가 얇아서 글씨가 비쳐요.
examples.en: This letter paper is thin, so the writing shows through.
I bought the letter paper and envelopes together.

explain: 편지를 쓰는 종이를 말하고, 짝말은 '편지봉투'예요. 보통 문구점에서 '편지지 세트'로 같이 팔아요.
explain_en: This is the paper you write a letter on, and its partner word is '편지봉투' (envelope). They are commonly sold together as a '편지지 세트' at stationery stores.

examples.ko: 미확인 메일이 쌓여서 편지함이 가득 찼어요.
examples.en: Unread emails piled up and the mailbox is full.

examples.ko: 편지함에 새 메일이 세 통 도착했어요.
examples.en: Three new emails arrived in the mailbox.
While cleaning up my mailbox, I found an old email.

examples.ko: 중요한 메일은 별도 편지함으로 옮겨 놓아요.
examples.en: I move important emails to a separate mailbox.
Spam emails were automatically deleted from the mailbox.
A notice popped up saying the mailbox is out of space.

explain: 이메일에서는 '받은편지함', '보낸편지함'처럼 쓰는 일이 많아요. 집 앞에 달린 우편물 상자는 보통 '우편함'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In email you often see it in '받은편지함' (inbox) and '보낸편지함' (sent mail). The box for physical mail at your home is usually called '우편함'.

examples.en: On autumn nights you can hear the sound of grass insects.
Grass insects chirped outside the window all night.
Grass insects are hopping around in the meadow.

examples.ko: 창문을 열었더니 풀벌레 소리가 시원하게 들렸어요.
examples.en: When I opened the window, the sound of insects came in refreshingly.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 풀벌레 소리를 들으며 잠이 들어요.
examples.en: In the countryside, I fall asleep listening to grass insects.
The child is rummaging through the grass to catch insects.

explain: 풀숲에 사는 작은 벌레를 두루 가리키는 말이라, 귀뚜라미 같은 벌레를 하나하나 말하지 않고 소리와 분위기를 말할 때 편해요. '풀벌레 소리'라는 표현이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It covers small insects living in the grass in general, so it is handy when you talk about the sound or mood without naming each insect, such as a cricket. The phrase '풀벌레 소리' comes up often.

examples.en: On my way home from work, I got a whole fried chicken to go.
I'll order half fried and half seasoned chicken.
The fried chicken at this place is crispy and delicious.
I like fried chicken more than seasoned chicken.
This place has a special sauce for its fried chicken.
Fried chicken loses its crispiness when it cools.

explain: 그냥 '치킨'이라고 줄여 말하는 일이 많고, 말할 때는 '후라이드'라고도 해요. 주문할 때 '양념치킨'과 나눠서 고르는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: People often just say '치킨', and in speech it is also pronounced '후라이드'. When ordering, you often choose between this and '양념치킨' (seasoned chicken).

examples.en: On weekends I go to a PC bang with my friends.

examples.ko: 피시방에서 게임을 하다가 시간이 훌쩍 갔어요.
examples.en: Time flew by while I was playing games at the PC bang.

examples.ko: 집 컴퓨터가 고장 나서 피시방을 이용했어요.
examples.en: My home computer broke, so I used a PC bang.
How much is the PC bang fee for one hour?

examples.ko: 학교 근처 피시방은 항상 학생들로 붐벼요.
examples.en: The PC bang near school is always crowded with students.
I heard the ramen at PC bangs is surprisingly good.

explain: 'PC방'이라고 쓰는 일이 많고, 한국의 피시방은 인터넷 카페보다는 주로 게임을 하러 가는 곳이에요. '피시방 가다/피시방에서 놀다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is often written 'PC방', and a Korean PC bang is mainly a place to go play games rather than a cafe for browsing. You say '피시방 가다' or '피시방에서 놀다'.

examples.ko: 눈이 내려서 온 동네가 하얘지는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the whole neighborhood turn white as the snow fell.

examples.ko: 긴장하면 머릿속이 하얘지고 아무 말도 안 나와요.
examples.en: When I get nervous, my mind goes blank and I can't say anything.
Does your skin get whiter if you apply this cream?

examples.ko: 머리카락이 하얘지기 시작해서 염색을 할까 고민이에요.
examples.en: My hair is starting to turn white, so I am thinking about dyeing it.

examples.ko: 표백제를 쓰면 하얘지긴 하지만 옷감이 상해요.
examples.en: Bleach does make clothes whiter, but it damages the fabric.
I endured it even though the pain made my face go pale.

explain: '하얗다'가 ㅎ 불규칙이라 '하얘요, 하얘졌어요'처럼 모양이 바뀌어요. 눈, 머리카락처럼 색이 변할 때뿐 아니라 놀라거나 아파서 얼굴이 창백해질 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 면접에서 질문을 듣는 순간 머릿속이 하얘졌어요.
phrases.en: The moment I heard the question in the interview, my mind went blank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀라거나 긴장해서 아무 생각도 나지 않는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where you are so startled or nervous that no thoughts come to mind.

explain_en: '하얗다' is an ㅎ-irregular verb, so the form changes as in '하얘요' and '하얘졌어요'. It is used not only for color changes like snow or hair, but also when your face goes pale from shock or pain.

examples.en: I was startled when a phone call suddenly came in the middle of the night.
The baby woke up and cried in the middle of the night.
The dead of night is quiet, so I end up thinking a lot.
Seoul's night view in the dead of night is really beautiful.
When it became the dead of night, the street grew quiet.
Yesterday I studied for the exam until the dead of night.

explain: 밤이 가장 깊은 때를 말하고, '한밤중'이라고도 해요. 늦은 저녁이나 새벽보다 더 깊은 밤 느낌이라 '한밤에 전화하다'처럼 놀랍거나 예의에 어긋나는 일과 같이 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the deepest part of the night and is also said as '한밤중'. It feels deeper than late evening or dawn, so it often appears with surprising or impolite things, like calling someone in the middle of the night.

examples.en: I took my foreign friend to a Korean restaurant.
There are many good Korean restaurants in this neighborhood.
I had lunch at the Korean restaurant in front of my office.
This Korean restaurant's menu also has bibimbap.

examples.ko: 부모님과 함께 갈 조용한 한식당을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I am looking for a quiet Korean restaurant to go to with my parents.
I like Korean restaurants because they bring out many side dishes.

explain: 한국 음식을 파는 식당 전체를 두루 말해요. 해외에서 한국 음식점을 말할 때 특히 자주 쓰고, 코스로 나오는 '한정식집'과는 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It broadly means any restaurant serving Korean food, and it is handy when talking about Korean restaurants abroad. It is a bit different from a '한정식집', which serves full-course Korean meals.

examples.en: In the morning, the sun came out from behind the clouds.

examples.ko: 아이가 해님을 그리고 웃는 얼굴을 넣었어요.
examples.en: The child drew the sun and gave it a smiling face.
Thanks to the sun, the laundry dried quickly.

examples.ko: 해님, 달님 이야기를 아이에게 읽어 줬어요.
examples.en: I read the child the story of the sun and the moon.
It is a baby who smiles as brightly as the sun.
In the fairy tale, the sun and the wind made a bet.

explain: '해'에 '님'을 붙여 해를 사람처럼 다정하게 부르는 말이에요. 동화, 동요, 아이에게 하는 말에서 잘 나오고, 어른이 날씨를 말할 때는 보통 그냥 '해'라고 해요. '달님'과 짝이에요.
explain_en: Adding '님' to '해' addresses the sun warmly, as if it were a person. It shows up in fairy tales, children's songs and talk with kids, while adults usually just say '해' when discussing the weather. Its partner word is '달님'.

examples.en: The autumn fields are all golden.
I received a gold-colored ring as a gift.
That doll has golden hair.

examples.ko: 이 포장지는 빨간색과 황금색이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: Red and gold go well together on this wrapping paper.
The bread was baked to a golden brown.

examples.ko: 황금색은 화려해 보여서 축제 장식에 써요.
examples.en: Gold looks splendid, so it is used for festival decorations.

explain: '금색'이나 '금빛'과 비슷하지만, 황금색은 노란빛이 도는 금 느낌이에요. 벼가 익은 들판, 노을, 노릇하게 구운 빵처럼 반짝이는 노란색을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is close to '금색' and '금빛', but '황금색' has a yellowish gold feel. It suits shiny yellow things like ripe rice fields, sunsets and golden-brown baked bread.

examples.en: The sky has been clouding over since the afternoon.

examples.ko: 말을 돌려서 하면 뜻이 흐려지기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you speak in a roundabout way, the meaning easily becomes unclear.

examples.ko: 눈이 나빠서 멀리 있는 글자가 흐려지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My eyesight is bad, so faraway letters seem to blur.

examples.ko: 시간이 지나면 기억이 점점 흐려지게 돼요.
examples.en: As time passes, memories gradually fade.
My vision, which had been hazy like fog, gradually cleared.
If the weather turns cloudy, bring an umbrella.

explain: '날씨가 흐리다'는 지금 상태이고, '흐려지다'는 점점 그렇게 변하는 과정이에요. 날씨뿐 아니라 기억, 시야, 경계가 분명하지 않게 될 때도 쓰고, 반대는 '맑아지다'나 '선명해지다'예요.
explain_en: '날씨가 흐리다' is the current state, while '흐려지다' is the process of gradually becoming so. It is used not only for weather but also when memory, vision or boundaries become unclear, and the opposites are '맑아지다' and '선명해지다'.

examples.ko: 우리 형은 힘세서 무거운 짐도 번쩍 들어요.
examples.en: My older brother is strong, so he lifts even heavy loads with ease.

examples.ko: 힘센 사람이 와서 이 상자를 좀 옮겨 주세요.
examples.en: Could a strong person come and move this box?

examples.ko: 아빠는 어릴 때 동네에서 제일 힘세다고 소문났어요.
examples.en: Dad was said to be the strongest in the neighborhood when he was young.
That puppy is really strong even though it is small.
Even with age, Grandpa is still strong.

examples.ko: 저 사람은 겉보기와 달리 별로 힘세지 않아요.
examples.en: Unlike how he looks, that person isn't very strong.

explain: '힘이 세다'를 한 단어로 붙여 쓴 형용사라서, 사람 앞에서는 '힘센 사람'처럼 '힘센'이 돼요. 반대는 '약하다'이고, 몸이 튼튼하다는 말과는 조금 달리 '힘이 강하다'는 데 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is '힘이 세다' fused into one adjective, so before a noun it becomes '힘센', as in '힘센 사람'. The opposite is '약하다', and it focuses on physical power rather than simply having a healthy body.
